summary: Backend-only readonly review completed with isolated diagnostic tests. Core hypotheses around webhook/session recovery, welcome idempotency, scheduler claim handling, retry gaps, recovery-mode limits, and reply association were reproducibly validated. No application code was modified.

critical.issue: Inbound from child/unknown non-parent records recipient_sessions but _record_reply exits early (parent_id=None), so needs_inbound_click recovery/welcome resend path is unreachable.
Concurrent same event_key calls can both pass pre-check and both send (non-atomic claim between SELECT and UPSERT).
Scheduler skips event when care_send_claims.status != failed; async receipt failure updates message_logs but not claim, so slot can be stuck skipped.
Failed notification states are excluded from retry selector; async failed receipts are not drained/retried by queue worker.
Button effects update latest category/day log, not exact replied-to message_log_id/context row; can mutate wrong reminder row.
If resolve_meta_media_url returns None, audio message is recorded as non-voice text branch (blank body), causing incorrect reply classification/notification path.

critical.endpoint: webhook retry path for button side effects
critical.issue: If _apply_button_tap_effects fails after _record_reply commit, webhook retry hits duplicate path and permanently bypasses side effect.

minor.issue: At parent-local 22:05 with default window_end=22:00, eligible gate blocks watch run; post-window main warning does not fire.
Provider status=uncertain is not marked sent, so repeated reengagement attempts can resend uncertain template.
Resets reengagement_sent=false for every opener/template type update, enabling repeated nudges after later template sends.
messages validator reads recovery_mode before field parsed (field-order dependency), so Raksha recovery extra reminders are rejected.
Expired recovery_until is ignored; recovery messages still loaded/sent unless manually removed.
Single medicine schedule slot expands to multiple sends by medicine name at same time, causing schedule-slot vs send-count mismatch under reminder caps.
Health reminders outside parent window are correctly blocked_template; this is safe blocking but indicates incomplete out-of-window health template feature.
Plan entitlement source is payment_state.plan only; billing_access.access resolver is not consulted (source-level review).

action_items: Add atomic welcome claim (single-statement claim/update) and durable worker for pending/failed welcome_deliveries.
Reconcile scheduler claim state with async receipt failures; allow retry path for failed async deliveries.
Extend notification retry/drain policy to include failed asynchronous statuses with bounded retry logic.
Bind button effects and family context updates to exact replied message (message_log_id/context.sid), not latest category.
Handle unresolved audio media URL explicitly as media failure, not blank text reply.
Make button side effects idempotent and replay-safe across webhook retries.
Fix ScheduleInput recovery_mode/messages validation order and enforce recovery_until expiry in schedule loader/worker.
Align entitlement checks across scheduler and billing_access.access to avoid quota divergence.
critical_code_review_comments: Multiple reliability paths remain source-coupled to optimistic synchronous outcomes; async provider failures are not fully modeled in retry/claim state transitions.
Idempotency is inconsistent across inbound processing stages (commit-before-side-effect with duplicate short-circuit).
Several limits/eligibility checks derive from partial state (plan only, message category latest, window gate strictness) leading to silent drops/misattribution.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the same diagnostic suite with real asyncpg/redis dependencies enabled (without stubs) to validate against production-like import/runtime. Keep tests readonly; do not start live providers. Focus retest on webhook retry idempotency and async receipt retry semantics after fixes.
rca of the issue: Root pattern: state transitions are split across DB rows/tables without a single authoritative retry contract. Repro used isolated mocks to show claim/write ordering, fallback paths, and validator/load ordering mismatches. Mitigation direction: atomic claims + explicit finite-state machine for delivery/retry + exact context binding + deterministic validation order.
